title: Physical and Financial Conditions at Selected Mitchell-Lama Developments
plain_title: Conditions and spending at three Mitchell-Lama developments
agency: New York City Department of Housing Preservation and Development
what_they_audited: Whether Mitchell-Lama developments supervised by the Department of Housing Preservation and Development are maintained in a way that protects residents' health and safety and whether their funds are used for intended purposes. The audit covered January 2019 through April 2025.
background: The Mitchell-Lama program, created in 1955, provides affordable rental and co-op housing for middle-income families, and the department supervises 92 city developments with about 46,787 units. The audit sampled three developments: Clinton Towers in Manhattan, Evergreen Gardens in the Bronx and Tivoli Towers in Brooklyn.

findings.plain: The department needs to improve its oversight. Management at all three sampled developments failed to provide a safe and clean living environment and spent development funds on activities not directly related to operations.
findings.quote: Management at all three sampled developments failed to provide a safe and clean living environment

findings.plain: Auditors observed hazardous conditions across the three developments, including facade damage, fire doors that did not close, units with mold, water damage and peeling paint and a day care tenant with mouse droppings in classrooms.
findings.quote: façade damage; non-working self-closing/fire doors; units with mold, water damage, and peeling paint; and a commercial tenant (day care) with mouse droppings in classrooms

findings.plain: About $163,862 in transactions from 2019 through 2024 were unrelated to normal operations or inadequately supported, including $114,288 in non-mandated bonuses, holiday events and gratuities and $49,574 in expenses without invoices or canceled checks.
findings.quote: approximately $163,862 in transactions for the period from January 2019 through December 2024 that were either unrelated to normal operations or inadequately supported

findings.plain: Managing agents at Clinton and Tivoli Towers lost an estimated $327,514 in rent from units that sat vacant for more than 120 days.
findings.quote: managing agents were unable to collect $327,514 in unrealized rental income from units that remained vacant for more than 120 days

findings.plain: All three developments paid vendors more than $100,000 in aggregate without notifying the department as required, and Evergreen hired five such vendors with no department approval and no evidence of competitive bidding.
findings.quote: Evergreen contracted with five vendors with payments over $100,000 without receiving HPD approval and no evidence of competitive bidding.

recommendations: Improve monitoring of the three developments, verifying that managing agents conduct annual unit inspections, complete related reports, correct deficiencies and keep self-closing fire doors working.
Ensure immediate corrective action when hazardous conditions are identified.
Develop and implement policies and procedures on bonus and gratuity payments.
Ensure managing agents operate the developments in a fiscally sound way by adequately reviewing expenses and supporting documentation during annual reviews.
Periodically review expenses to identify vendor payments that reach $100,000 in a fiscal year and confirm the department approved them and contracts were competitively bid.
